subtype: Approach: cutting losses on an unused commitment [Revision]
passage: We were going through last quarter's bank statements one evening, me with a highlighter and Siddharth with a bowl of roasted chana, when I found three lines that made me stop. Membership at a gym, and two video subscriptions. Nobody in the flat had used any of them since spring. I'm Ankita, by the way. My first thought was, but we paid for the whole year of the gym! It felt like throwing away the money already spent. Siddharth said, "That money's gone either way. The only question is whether we keep paying." So we cancelled all three that same night. The monthly amount went into a small travel fund, and I checked it last week: enough for a long weekend in the hills. I still wince about the gym, but less than the monthly wince.

qa.q: Where did the money from the cancelled plans go?
qa.a: It went into a small travel fund.

qa.q: What did Ankita feel when first seeing the gym charge?
qa.a: Ankita felt reluctant to let go, since cancelling seemed like throwing away money already spent.

qa.q: What could Ankita and Siddharth do to catch this earlier?
qa.a: They could go through their statements every few months and cancel anything nobody uses.

qa.q: How does Siddharth see the money already spent?
qa.a: Siddharth sees it as gone either way, so the only question is whether to keep paying.

grounding: Ankita and Siddharth find a gym and two video plans nobody uses, cancel them despite the money already spent and redirect the amount to a travel fund.

subtype: Approach: cutting losses on an unused commitment [Revision]
passage:
I share a wall and a balcony with Chetan and Neelam, so I hear more than I should. Last Sunday they had their bank statements spread across the balcony table, and I heard Chetan say, "Wait. We're still paying for the gym?"
They joined in January. From my side of the balcony, neither of them has left the house in running shoes since February. Then Neelam found two streaming plans. "Which one do we even watch?" "Neither, since the cricket ended."
Chetan said, "But we paid the joining fee. If we cancel now, that's wasted." Neelam said, "It's already wasted. The question is next month." He was quiet for a bit. Then I heard typing.
On Monday there was a jar on their shelf labelled Hampi, and Chetan told me they had cancelled all three. He looked a little sheepish. Neelam looked pleased.
— Hafsa

qa.q: What was the jar on the shelf labelled?
What was Chetan feeling when he said the joining fee would be wasted?
qa.a: He felt reluctant and a little regretful, not wanting to accept that the money already spent was gone.

qa.q: What else could the couple do to catch unused plans sooner?
qa.a: They could go through their statements together every few months and ask of each plan whether they would sign up for it today.

qa.q: How does Neelam see the gym joining fee?
qa.a: Neelam sees it as already spent; what matters to her is whether they keep paying next month.

grounding: It shows a couple finding an unused gym membership and two streaming plans, cancelling them despite the sunk cost and putting the money toward a trip.

subtype: Approach: cutting losses on an unused commitment [Revision]
passage:
Saturday, 3 August. Sharmila and her sister Ganga sit in their Chennai flat with a highlighter and three months of bank statements. Ganga circles a gym membership, a music plan and a movie plan. "Who uses these?" Sharmila groans. "The gym is mine. I went four times."
Sunday, 4 August. Sharmila hesitates. "If I cancel the gym, the joining fee is gone." Ganga says, "It's gone either way." That evening Sharmila cancels all three, grumbling, and sets up a small monthly transfer of the same amount into a new pot they call Andaman.
Friday, 20 December. Ganga checks the Andaman pot. There is enough for two ferry tickets and a guesthouse deposit. Sharmila laughs. "Best gym I never went to."

qa.q: What did they call the new pot?
Why did Sharmila hesitate on Sunday?
qa.a: Sharmila felt reluctant and regretful about losing the joining fee already paid for the gym.

qa.q: What made the change stick, and what else could help?
qa.a: Moving the same amount straight into the Andaman pot gave the money a new purpose; checking statements every few months would catch the next unused plan.

qa.q: How does Ganga see the cancelled gym?
qa.a: Ganga sees the fee as gone either way, and by December can watch the pot turn into ferry tickets 😊

grounding: It shows sisters finding an unused gym membership and two streaming plans, cancelling them despite the sunk cost and redirecting the money into a travel fund.
